subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh in:
explanation: Muhammad bin Qasim led the Umayyad expedition that conquered Sindh in 712 AD, the first major Muslim conquest in the subcontinent.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Muhammad bin Qasim was sent to Sindh by:
explanation: Hajjaj bin Yusuf, the Umayyad governor of Iraq, dispatched his young kinsman Muhammad bin Qasim against Raja Dahir.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The first city captured by Muhammad bin Qasim in Sindh was:
explanation: The port of Debal, near modern Karachi, fell first; Muhammad bin Qasim then advanced up the Indus to Aror, Brahmanabad and Multan.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The ruler of Sindh defeated by Muhammad bin Qasim was:
explanation: Raja Dahir ruled Sindh from Aror and was killed fighting Muhammad bin Qasim; Jaipal and Anandpal fought Mahmud of Ghazni.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Mahmud of Ghazni's most famous raid in India was on the temple of:
explanation: Mahmud's attack on the Somnath temple in Gujarat (1025–26) became the best-known of his many expeditions into India.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Kitab-ul-Hind, a detailed study of Indian society and sciences, was written by:
explanation: Al-Biruni, who came to India with Mahmud of Ghazni, studied Sanskrit and wrote Kitab-ul-Hind on Indian religion, customs and sciences.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: In the Second Battle of Tarain (1192), Muhammad Ghori defeated:
explanation: Ghori's victory over Prithviraj Chauhan at Tarain in 1192 opened north India to permanent Muslim rule.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Delhi Sultanate was founded in 1206 by:
explanation: After Muhammad Ghori's death in 1206, his slave-general Qutb-ud-Din Aibak became the first Sultan of Delhi, founding the Slave (Mamluk) dynasty.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The construction of the Qutb Minar in Delhi was completed by:
explanation: Qutb-ud-Din Aibak began the minaret but completed only its first storey; his successor Iltutmish added the upper storeys.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Razia Sultana, the only woman to rule the Delhi Sultanate, was the daughter of:
explanation: Iltutmish nominated his daughter Razia as his successor, and she ruled Delhi from 1236 to 1240.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which Sultan of Delhi introduced strict market and price controls?
explanation: Alauddin Khilji fixed prices of grain and other goods and set up market officials to maintain his large standing army cheaply.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which Sultan transferred his capital from Delhi to Daulatabad?
explanation: Muhammad bin Tughlaq moved the capital to Daulatabad (Devagiri) in the Deccan, an experiment that failed and was reversed.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Mughal Empire was founded after the First Battle of Panipat in:
explanation: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodhi at Panipat in 1526, ending the Delhi Sultanate and founding Mughal rule.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: At the First Battle of Panipat, Babur defeated:
explanation: Ibrahim Lodhi, the last Sultan of Delhi, was killed at Panipat in 1526; Babur defeated Rana Sanga the next year at Khanwa.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Babur wrote his memoirs, Tuzk-e-Babri, in:
explanation: Babur wrote the Baburnama in his native Chaghatai Turkish; it was translated into Persian in Akbar's reign.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The road from Sonargaon in Bengal to the north-west, later called the Grand Trunk Road, was built by:
explanation: Sher Shah Suri built the long highway (Sadak-e-Azam) with sarais along it, which the British later called the Grand Trunk Road.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The silver coin called the "rupiya" was introduced by:
explanation: Sher Shah Suri issued a standard silver rupiya, which the Mughals retained and which gave its name to the rupee.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Din-i-Ilahi was introduced by:
explanation: Akbar announced Din-i-Ilahi in 1582 as an eclectic creed of his court; it found few followers and ended with him.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Mansabdari system, which graded nobles and officers by rank, was organised by:
explanation: Akbar organised his nobility into mansabs (ranks) that fixed each officer's pay and the troops he had to maintain.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The title "Mujaddid Alf Sani" is given to:
explanation: Sheikh Ahmad Sirhindi was called the "Renewer of the Second Millennium" for opposing Akbar's religious innovations and reviving orthodox Islam.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Sheikh Ahmad Sirhindi belonged to which Sufi order?
explanation: Mujaddid Alf Sani was a disciple of Khawaja Baqi Billah and spread the Naqshbandi order, which stressed adherence to the Shariah.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Fatawa-e-Alamgiri, a compilation of Hanafi law, was prepared under the patronage of:
explanation: Aurangzeb Alamgir commissioned a board of scholars to compile Fatawa-e-Alamgiri as a code of Islamic law for his empire.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Badshahi Mosque in Lahore was built by:
explanation: Aurangzeb built the Badshahi Mosque in 1673–74 opposite the Lahore Fort; Shah Jahan is remembered for the Shalimar Gardens and the Taj Mahal.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The last Mughal emperor, Bahadur Shah Zafar, was exiled after 1857 to:
explanation: The British tried Bahadur Shah Zafar for his role in 1857 and exiled him to Rangoon in Burma, where he died in 1862.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: In the Third Battle of Panipat (1761), Ahmad Shah Abdali defeated the:
explanation: Abdali's victory over the Marathas at Panipat in 1761 checked Maratha expansion into northern India.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which Muslim scholar invited Ahmad Shah Abdali to check the power of the Marathas?
explanation: Shah Waliullah wrote to Ahmad Shah Abdali urging him to save the Muslims of India from the Marathas, which led to the Third Battle of Panipat.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Shah Waliullah translated the Holy Qur'an into:
explanation: Shah Waliullah translated the Qur'an into Persian, the literary language of the time, so that educated Muslims could read it directly.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Hujjat Allah al-Baligha is the best-known work of:
explanation: Shah Waliullah's Hujjat Allah al-Baligha explains the wisdom behind Islamic teachings and is his most influential book.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: At the Battle of Plassey (1757), the East India Company defeated:
explanation: Robert Clive defeated Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah of Bengal at Plassey, helped by the treachery of Mir Jafar.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Whose betrayal enabled Robert Clive to win the Battle of Plassey?
explanation: Siraj-ud-Daulah's commander Mir Jafar held back his troops in return for being made Nawab; Mir Sadiq later betrayed Tipu Sultan.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: After the Battle of Buxar (1764), the Mughal emperor granted the East India Company the diwani (revenue rights) of:
explanation: Under the Treaty of Allahabad (1765), Shah Alam II gave the Company the diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa, making it the real ruler there.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Tipu Sultan was martyred in 1799 while defending:
explanation: Tipu Sultan died fighting at his capital Seringapatam in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Treaty of Seringapatam (1792) was signed between Tipu Sultan and:
explanation: After the Third Anglo-Mysore War, Governor-General Lord Cornwallis forced Tipu to cede half his territory under this treaty.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Doctrine of Lapse, under which states without a natural heir were annexed, was applied by:
explanation: Lord Dalhousie annexed Satara, Jhansi, Nagpur and others by refusing to recognise adopted heirs, a policy that fed the resentment behind 1857.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Subsidiary Alliance system was introduced by:
explanation: Lord Wellesley made Indian rulers keep Company troops at their own cost and accept a British Resident, bringing them under Company control.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Permanent Settlement of land revenue in Bengal (1793) was introduced by:
explanation: Cornwallis fixed revenue permanently with zamindars, a system that dispossessed many Muslim landholding families in Bengal.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Syed Ahmad Shaheed and Shah Ismail Shaheed were martyred in 1831 at:
explanation: The two leaders of the Mujahideen movement fell fighting Sikh forces at Balakot in May 1831.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Jihad movement of Syed Ahmad Barelvi was mainly directed against:
o: Sikh rule in the Punjab and the frontier
explanation: Syed Ahmad Barelvi set up his base in the frontier region to free Muslims from Ranjit Singh's Sikh rule.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Faraizi Movement was launched in Bengal by:
explanation: Haji Shariatullah started the Faraizi Movement among Bengali peasants after returning from Makkah.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: After Haji Shariatullah, the Faraizi Movement was led by his son:
explanation: Dudu Mian (Muhsin-ud-Din Ahmad) organised the Faraizis against the exactions of Hindu zamindars and indigo planters.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Faraizi Movement took its name from its emphasis on:
o: Paying land revenue to the Company
explanation: Faraiz means the obligatory duties of Islam; the movement called on Bengali Muslims to observe them and give up un-Islamic customs.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Titu Mir, who built a bamboo fort to resist landlords and the British, led his movement in:
explanation: Titu Mir's bamboo fort at Narikelbaria in Bengal was destroyed by British troops in 1831.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan analysed the causes of the 1857 uprising in:
explanation: In Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind Sir Syed argued that the revolt resulted from British policies and the absence of Indians in the legislature, not a Muslim conspiracy.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The foundation stone of the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College, Aligarh, was laid in 1877 by:
explanation: Viceroy Lord Lytton laid the foundation stone of the MAO College in January 1877, two years after the school had opened.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The MAO College was raised to the status of Aligarh Muslim University in:
explanation: The long campaign for a Muslim university succeeded in 1920, when the MAO College became Aligarh Muslim University.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded the Scientific Society in 1864 at:
explanation: Sir Syed established the Scientific Society at Ghazipur to translate Western works into Urdu; it later moved with him to Aligarh.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The journal Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq was launched by:
explanation: Sir Syed started Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq in 1870 to reform the social and religious outlook of Muslims.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Muhammadan Educational Conference, founded by Sir Syed in 1886, aimed mainly to:
o: Unite Muslim ulema against the British
explanation: The Conference met annually in different cities to promote modern education; the Muslim League was later founded at its 1906 session.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Hindi–Urdu controversy that convinced Sir Syed that Hindus and Muslims could not remain one nation began in 1867 at:
explanation: Hindu demands at Banaras in 1867 to replace Urdu in the Persian script with Hindi in Devanagari led Sir Syed to speak of two separate nations.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Why did Sir Syed Ahmad Khan advise Muslims not to join the Indian National Congress?
o: He wanted Muslims to join the Muslim League
He opposed all contact with Hindus
He feared majority rule would subordinate the Muslim minority
He considered politics forbidden in Islam
explanation: Sir Syed believed that representative government on a majority basis would place Muslims under permanent Hindu domination, so he urged them to concentrate on education.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Sir Syed's Khutbat-e-Ahmadiya was written in reply to the book on the Holy Prophet (PBUH) by:
explanation: Sir Syed travelled to England and wrote Khutbat-e-Ahmadiya to answer William Muir's hostile "Life of Mahomet".

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Urdu Defence Association was formed in 1900 to oppose an order of the United Provinces government by:
explanation: When Lieutenant-Governor MacDonnell gave Hindi official status in the UP courts in 1900, Mohsin-ul-Mulk organised the Urdu Defence Association in protest.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Darul Uloom Deoband was founded by:
explanation: Maulana Muhammad Qasim Nanautvi, with Maulana Rashid Ahmad Gangohi, founded the Deoband seminary in 1866.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The main objective of Darul Uloom Deoband was to:
o: Preserve traditional Islamic learning and train ulema
explanation: After 1857 Deoband sought to protect Muslims' religious identity by teaching the traditional Islamic sciences, independent of government support.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which Deobandi scholar supported the Pakistan Movement and headed the Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam formed in 1945?
explanation: Unlike Hussain Ahmad Madani's pro-Congress Jamiat Ulema-e-Hind, Shabbir Ahmad Usmani led the pro-League Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Nadwat-ul-Ulema, founded in the 1890s, is located at:
explanation: The Nadwat-ul-Ulema established its seminary, Darul Uloom Nadwatul Ulama, at Lucknow.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Nadwat-ul-Ulema sought to:
o: Replace religious education with Western sciences
Combine traditional religious learning with useful modern knowledge
Revive Persian as the language of administration
explanation: Nadwa aimed at a middle path between Aligarh's modernism and Deoband's traditionalism, reforming the syllabus while keeping religious foundations.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Seerat-un-Nabi, begun by Maulana Shibli Nomani, was completed by:
explanation: Shibli died after writing the first volumes; his pupil Syed Sulaiman Nadvi completed the work.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Sindh Madressatul Islam, Karachi, where Quaid-i-Azam studied, was founded by:
explanation: Hassan Ali Effendi founded the Sindh Madressatul Islam in 1885 to provide modern education to Sindhi Muslims.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Islamia College Peshawar was founded in 1913 through the efforts of:
explanation: Sahibzada Abdul Qayyum Khan, with Sir George Roos-Keppel, established Islamia College to bring modern education to the frontier.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Anjuman-i-Himayat-i-Islam, which ran Islamia College and many schools, was established in 1884 at:
explanation: Founded in Lahore, the Anjuman spread modern and religious education among Punjabi Muslims and hosted Iqbal's early recitations.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Central National Muhammadan Association (1877) was founded by:
explanation: Syed Ameer Ali founded this Calcutta-based association, one of the first Muslim political bodies, to present Muslim demands to the government.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The War of Independence of 1857 began at:
explanation: Sepoys rose at Meerut on 10 May 1857 and marched to Delhi, where they proclaimed Bahadur Shah Zafar their leader.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The immediate cause of the War of Independence of 1857 was:
explanation: The new Enfield cartridges were rumoured to be greased with cow and pig fat, offending both Hindu and Muslim sepoys; deeper causes included annexations.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Through the Government of India Act 1858, the administration of India was transferred to:
explanation: The 1858 Act ended East India Company rule and placed India directly under the Crown, acting through a Secretary of State.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The first Viceroy of India after the 1858 transfer of power was:
explanation: Lord Canning, Governor-General during the 1857 uprising, became the first Viceroy when the Crown took over.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Indian National Congress was founded in:
explanation: The Indian National Congress held its first session at Bombay in December 1885.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Indian National Congress was founded by:
explanation: Allan Octavian Hume, a retired British civil servant, organised the Congress as a forum for educated Indians.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Bengal was partitioned in 1905 by Viceroy:
explanation: Lord Curzon divided Bengal for administrative reasons, creating the Muslim-majority province of Eastern Bengal and Assam.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The partition of Bengal was annulled in:
explanation: King George V announced the annulment at the Delhi Durbar of 1911, a decision that deeply disappointed Muslims.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The capital of the new province of Eastern Bengal and Assam (1905) was:
explanation: Dacca became the provincial capital, bringing development and opportunities to the Muslims of eastern Bengal.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Hindu opposition to the partition of Bengal took the form of:
o: The Swadeshi movement and boycott of British goods
explanation: Hindus launched the Swadeshi campaign, boycotting British goods, which eventually led the government to reverse the partition.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Along with annulling the partition of Bengal in 1911, the British shifted the capital of India from Calcutta to:
explanation: The Delhi Durbar of 1911 announced both the annulment and the transfer of the capital to Delhi.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Simla Deputation of 1906 was led by:
explanation: Aga Khan III led the 35-member Muslim deputation that met the Viceroy at Simla on 1 October 1906.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Simla Deputation presented its demands to Viceroy:
explanation: Lord Minto received the deputation sympathetically and assured it that Muslim political rights would be safeguarded.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The main demand of the Simla Deputation was:
o: Annulment of the partition of Bengal
explanation: The deputation asked that Muslims elect their own representatives and be given weightage beyond their numbers.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Separate electorates for Muslims were first granted by the:
explanation: The Minto-Morley Reforms, enacted as the Indian Councils Act 1909, accepted the Simla Deputation's demand for separate electorates.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The All-India Muslim League was founded on 30 December 1906 at:
explanation: The League was formed at Dhaka during the annual session of the Muhammadan Educational Conference.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The resolution establishing the All-India Muslim League was moved at Dhaka by:
explanation: Nawab Salimullah of Dhaka, the host of the session, moved the resolution to create the League.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Dhaka meeting of 1906 at which the Muslim League was founded was presided over by:
explanation: Nawab Viqar-ul-Mulk chaired the session, while Nawab Salimullah moved the resolution.
